brandGuideClaims.outerShell: Burton says a Wide boot uses the same outer shell as its same-size Regular counterpart.
brandGuideClaims.liner: The guide describes stretch neoprene panels instead of foam around the midfoot/forefoot transition to provide more room.
selectionAdvice: Measure feet with a shop fitting tool and try several boots in person.
A wide street shoe marked EE or wider may benefit from Wide, but street-shoe width alone does not decide the fit.
All-day pressure, hot spots, blisters, or cold/numb toes are reasons to try Wide.
Bring riding socks, walk in securely fastened boots for at least 15 minutes, and check heel hold while flexing forward.
US 11 or larger is only a prompt to consider a wide snowboard, not a boot-width threshold.

limits: The Burton guide is brand-wide guidance and does not publish Photon 2027 last width in millimeters or foot-volume measurements.

The Photon-specific page confirms the exact 2027 Wide option, while construction details come from Burton's universal rule for every boot labeled Wide; the Photon page does not independently enumerate liner materials.
Do not interpret its same-shell statement as a shell-width increase or convert it to a millimeter difference.
Do not use US 11 board-width guidance as a rule for choosing boot width.
decision: Keep Regular/Wide as selectable fit options. The 2027 Photon page confirms the Wide variant, and Burton states its same-shell/stretch-neoprene-liner construction applies to any Burton boot labeled Wide; record this as application of a brand-wide published rule, not Photon-specific teardown or measurement. No absolute or relative millimeter width or foot-volume value is known.
